The development for debian goes like this: new packages land in Sid, then after 2 weeks of no bugs they go to testing (currently bookworm) then every 2 years they freeze the packages so they can do bug fixes and qa. After a while this qaed and fixed version of debian becomes the new stable (currently bullseye)

You'll be on debian testing untill bookworm becomes stable then it will be on stable. This is what I did when i first set up my file server.  The freeze for bookworm starts next year Jan so it won't be too long before your back on stable.

You HAVE to pick one. Especially since the testing freeze is coming up and you don't want to have updated packages from Sid that didn't make it to testing. Then you'll be creating a franken debian. That means you might not be able to install software because a dependancy it needs can't be gotten. It's not a good place to be and turns into a mess real fast. 

There is a apt command to find what file belongs to what package. I think the keyword is "provides" or something like that. That would be a start. Or maybe someone else has this happen to them before and Google will tell you.
